title: Ops Lifecycle Guides & Templates — Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendor, Travel
author: Asha Menon
content:
Overview

Purpose: This consolidated playbook provides short, practical procedures and ready-to-use templates for company-wide operational lifecycles: access & permissions, change management, data governance, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding & risk review, and employee travel. The intent is to reduce friction, accelerate approvals, and provide clear ownership for common transaction types.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and vendors interacting with company systems and data. Specialty flows for Dedicated/Private customer environments are linked at the end.

Owner & escalation
- Primary owner: Finance & Legal (policy stewardship, procurement, vendor risk)
- Day-to-day operations: IT/Platform (access provisioning, change deployments)
- Security owner: InfoSec (data classification, vendor security assessment)
- Escalation path: requestor -> manager -> policy owner -> CISO/CFO for exceptions

Quick reference (policy map)
| Area | Primary owner | Typical SLA | Mandatory approvers | Template location |
| Access & Permissions | IT/Platform | 3 business days standard; 4 hours emergency | Manager + Resource Owner | /templates/access-request.md |
| Change Management | Eng Platform | 48 hours for planned, 60 minutes for emergency ack | Service Owner + Eng Lead | /templates/change-request.yaml |
| Data Management | InfoSec | N/A (ongoing governance) | Data Owner + Security | /templates/data-classification.csv |
| Procurement & Expenses | Finance | PO within 5 business days | Budget Owner + Procurement | /templates/purchase-order.docx |
| Vendor Management | Finance-Legal | 7–10 business days for low-risk vendors | Procurement + Security | /templates/vendor-onboard.pdf |
| Travel | People Ops + Finance | Pre-approval 5 business days | Manager + People Ops | /templates/travel-request.html |

1) Access & Permissions
Purpose: Ensure least privilege, auditable approvals, and timely onboarding/offboarding.
Roles: Requestor, Manager (approver), Resource Owner (service owner), IT Fulfillment (provisioning), Audit Reviewer (quarterly).
Access tiers (examples)
- Tier 0: Public docs, no auth required
- Tier 1: Internal (view-only internal docs, Slack)
- Tier 2: Sensitive (customer metadata, non-PII infra configs)
- Tier 3: Regulated/Restricted (PII, customer data, keys)

Access request procedure (standard)
1. Requestor opens an Access Request in Jira (project: IT-ACCESS) using the Access Request template. Include justification, duration, and owner.
2. Manager approves in Jira (1–2 business days).
3. Resource Owner reviews and signs off (3 business days).
4. IT Fulfillment implements and records the change in the IAM audit log (S3://redwood-audit/iam).
5. Request auto-expires at specified duration; owners receive reminder 7 days before expiry.

Emergency access (approved temporary elevated access)
- Use the Emergency Access channel in PagerDuty; an on-call IT lead must acknowledge within 60 minutes and update the Jira ticket. Emergency access must be re-reviewed within 48 hours and converted to a standard access request or revoked.

Access review cadence
- Quarterly role reviews for Tier 2 and Tier 3 resources. Business unit leads must certify access lists to InfoSec. Failure to respond triggers a removal workflow after 14 days.

Template examples (available under /templates)
- access-request.md (fields: requester, manager, resource, justification, expiration, data-tier, business-impact)
- iam-policy-snippet.json (example allowed actions)

2) Change Management
Purpose: Prevent outages and data loss by making all impactful changes auditable and risk assessed.
Change categories
- Standard (low-risk routine ops, pre-approved steps)
- Normal (planned changes requiring risk assessment and approval)
- Emergency (outage, security patching; accelerate path)

Change process (Normal)
1. Create a Change Request using the change-request.yaml template in Confluence. Include rollback plan, testing steps, and expected impact window.
2. Risk classification (low/medium/high) performed by the Service Owner.
3. Approvals: Service Owner -> Engineering Lead -> Change Advisory Board (CAB) for high-risk (>5% error budget impact, >2 hour user-facing downtime). CAB meets daily at 09:30 for high/medium items.
4. Scheduling: change windows are Monday–Friday 02:00–06:00 PT for non-emergency infra changes.
5. Post-change validation: automated canary tests + 30-minute validation period. If regressions occur, execute rollback. Document results in the change ticket.

Emergency change process
- PagerDuty incident created + emergency change ticket. Incident commander authorizes immediate execution if rollback plan exists. Post-incident RCA required within 5 business days.

3) Data Management & Classification
Classification scheme
- PUBLIC: Safe for external distribution
- INTERNAL: Redwood staff only (non-sensitive)
- CONFIDENTIAL: Business-sensitive, internal use only
- RESTRICTED: Regulated data (PII, payment information, customer-provided sensitive data)

Handling rules summary
- Encryption: All CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED data must be encrypted at rest (KMS) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Storage: RESTRICTED data must not be stored in personal devices or unmanaged SaaS. Use Redwood-approved encrypted buckets or DBs only.
- Logging: Access to RESTRICTED data must be logged and reviewed monthly.
- Retention: Default retention is 365 days for logs, data retention by dataset defined in Data Catalog.

Data access request: follow Access & Permissions flow and add Data Owner review for CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED.

Breach & exfiltration reporting
- If suspected exfiltration: immediately notify InfoSec (security@redwood.ai) and open an incident. Customer-impact assessment within 24 hours. Legal engages for any regulated data.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Spend thresholds and approvals
- <= $2,500: Manager approval (expense report)
- $2,501–$25,000: Manager + Budget Owner + Procurement intake
- > $25,000: Manager + Budget Owner + Procurement + Legal + CFO review

PO & vendor purchase steps
1. Create a Purchase Request in Procurement Portal with business justification and vendor details. Attach SOW or quote if available.
2. Procurement verifies vendor status and assigns PO number within 5 business days.
3. Finance issues payment upon receipt of invoice and proof of delivery/service. Average payment terms: Net 30 unless otherwise contracted.

Expense policy highlights
- All travel and client entertainment expenses require itemized receipts. Use the Expense template and submit within 30 days of spend.
- Non-compliant expenses (personal items, upgrades without approval) are rejected.

Shared-cost and capital purchases
- Capital purchases (> $50k) require Finance forecasting approval and depreciation plan.

5) Vendor Management (Onboarding & Offboarding)
Onboarding checklist (minimum requirements)
1. Business vetting: legal entity, tax forms (W9/W8), references.
2. Security questionnaire: vendor completes Redwood security questionnaire (SaaS Vendors: questionnaire + penetration test or SOC2 report).
3. Contract review: Legal reviews standard terms, data residency, and indemnity clauses.
4. Procurement assigns vendor ID and payment terms.
5. Technical integration review: Architect reviews data flows and sets up least-privilege access.

Vendor risk tiers & timelines
- Low Risk (non-prod SaaS without customer data): 2–5 business days
- Medium Risk (production infra, limited customer data): 5–10 business days
- High Risk (handles RESTRICTED data): 10–20 business days + Security assessment & contractual safeguards

Offboarding
- Revoke all credentials, remove service accounts, and confirm data deletion or handoff. Confirm completion in Procurement Portal. Retain records per retention policy.

Vendor red flags (requires Legal escalation)
- Refusal to sign standard data processing addendum (DPA)
- No security attestations for vendors accessing customer data
- Unclear subcontractor chain or data export without controls

6) Travel Policy (Summary)
Booking and approvals
- Pre-approval required for any travel > $250. Submit Travel Request (link in templates) at least 5 business days prior.
- Flights: economy for trips < 6 hours; business with manager approval for > 6 hours on international flights.
- Hotels: mid-tier chain within per-diem cap; prefer negotiated vendor rates.
- Ride-sharing: preferred for last-mile transport; car rentals require business justification.

Per-diem and expenses
- Domestic per-diem cap: $75/day for meals and incidentals; international per country caps vary (see travel template). Receipts required for meals > $25.

Safety & insurance
- Employees must register travel for higher-risk locations with People Ops. Emergency contact and insurance coverage are handled via People Ops.

7) Templates & Implementation Aids
Location: /confluence/templates and the shared drive /templates/ops/
Available templates (editable)
- access-request.md (markdown form for direct Jira paste)
- change-request.yaml (structured change form + rollback section)
- data-classification.csv (spreadsheet for dataset owners)
- purchase-request.docx (PO request form)
- vendor-onboard.pdf (checklist and security questionnaire link)
- travel-request.html (web form that populates expense system)

Example snippets
- IAM policy (example)
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["s3:GetObject"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-internal/*"] }
  ]
}

Exception & change control for the playbook
- Any requested exception to these policies must be submitted via the Exception Request template and will be evaluated by the policy owner and either approved with compensating controls or rejected. Major changes to this document require review by Finance, InfoSec, and People Ops, and a 7-day comment period.
